jacket.definition: A jacket is a piece of clothing with long sleeves that you wear over a shirt. A jacket is not as long as a coat.
jacket.sentence: He took his phone from the pocket of his jacket.

jail.definition: A place where people who have done a crime or a suspected of having done a crime are kept.

job.definition: A job is an activity that you do, usually, regularly and for pay.
job.sentence: She got a good job as a manager in a book store.

join.definition: If someone joins two or more things, they bring them together.
join.sentence: I will join you on your walk.

joint.definition: A place where two things meet but are still able to move.
joint.sentence: It was the kind of joint you wouldn't want your boss to see you in.

joke.definition: If you tell a joke, you say something to make people laugh.
joke.sentence: Trevor's joke about the boring lexicographer was too funny.

journal.definition: A journal is a record of what is happening, usually written regularly (e.g., daily, weekly, monthly, etc.), often scientific.
journal.sentence: They published their study in the British Medical Journal.

journalist.definition: A journalist is a person who writes and reports the news.

journey.definition: A journey is a long trip.
journey.sentence: Timothy left on a long journey.

joy.definition: Joy is a feeling of great happiness and pleasure.
joy.sentence: They will be a source of strength and joy in your life.

judge.definition: A judge is a person who decides or chooses.

judgment.definition: Judgment is being able to make good choices.
judgment.sentence: You will need good judgment to decide on a school.

jump.definition: If you jump, you leave the ground completely.
jump.sentence: We used his car to jump ours.

jury.definition: A jury is a group of people who decide a court case's result.
jury.sentence: The jury says the person is not guilty.

just.definition: When you just do something, you only did that thing.
just.sentence: He was hungry, and he just wanted a good meal.

justice.definition: You need justice when you have been treated unfairly, cheated, hurt, or denied your basic rights by others.
justice.sentence: To have justice means treating every single person the same way, no matter how they look, where they come from, or what they believe.

justify.definition: If you justify something that people think is bad, you explain why it was good or why it had to happen that way.
justify.sentence: One problem in music education is always having to justify our existence to other teachers.
